title: Cache Lifecycle and Invalidation
readerIntent: Understand lookup, population, invalidation, import/export interaction, and recovery.
priorKnowledge: Know the logical cache channel and authoritative source.
owner: Owning capability, cache policy, and configured provider
summary: A read computes a tenant-safe key, checks eligibility, returns a valid hit or loads the authority, and invalidates or refreshes entries after owned state changes.

sections.heading: Read flow
items: Resolve tenant, principal, module, operation, and channel.
Apply the centralized cacheability policy.
Build a bounded namespaced key without sensitive raw values.
Return a valid hit or load from the authoritative owner.
Store only eligible results with configured TTL and serialization.
Record safe hit, miss, bypass, provider, and latency signals.

sections.heading: Invalidation
items: The owning successful state transition emits or invokes its invalidation contract.
Single-process providers clear local entries; distributed providers propagate required invalidation.
If invalidation assurance is insufficient for a security-sensitive channel, fail closed or bypass cache.
Restart, reconnect, and topology changes must not make cached data authoritative.

sections.heading: Data exchange
paragraphs: A finalized import invalidates or refreshes affected cache entries through the same ownership contracts as ordinary saves. Export may read through authorized services, but correctness cannot depend on a stale cache and export must never dump cache storage as authoritative data.

sections.heading: Population strategies
items: Cache-aside loads on a miss and stores an eligible result.
Read-through delegates loading through the cache contract where supported.
Write invalidation removes entries after authoritative success.
Write refresh recomputes only when ordering and cost are safe.
Prewarming is optional and never replaces readiness of the authority.

sections.heading: TTL and staleness
paragraphs: TTL limits how long an entry survives without invalidation; it does not guarantee freshness. Select it from business tolerance, change frequency, load, and invalidation assurance.
Non-expiring entries require a stronger invalidation and representation-version contract and should be rare.

sections.heading: Failure behavior
items: Provider unavailable before lookup: bypass or fail according to channel policy.
Load authority unavailable: return its normalized failure, not an invented stale success unless explicitly allowed.
Put failure after authoritative read: return the valid result and record cache degradation when policy permits.
Invalidation failure: retry, bypass, or fail closed according to sensitivity.
Reconnect or provider change: prevent incompatible old entries from becoming valid.

sections.heading: Concurrency
paragraphs: Concurrent misses can create a stampede. Channels may use bounded coalescing, jittered expiry, or locks where provider semantics are qualified. Locks themselves require deadlines and failure recovery.
Consume-once behavior requires an atomic provider operation; read followed by delete is not equivalent.

sections.heading: Lifecycle verification
items: Hit, miss, bypass, expiry, and non-expiring behavior.
Create, update, delete, publishing, and import invalidation.
Tenant, principal, locale, catalog, and permission isolation.
Concurrent miss, stampede control, and atomic consume.
Provider outage, invalidation failure, reconnect, restart, and topology change.
Normal operation with caching disabled.
